quote: We now investigate a first-order stochastic dominance property satisfied by the HLIL distribution, according to the concept described in [19]. Let φ1 = (α1, λ1, β1) and φ2 = (α2, λ2, β2). Then, if α2 ≤ α1, λ1 ≤ λ2 and β1 ≤ β2, we have F(x; φ1) ≤ F(x; φ2).  (7)  The proof of (7) is given in the Appendix. Thus, under the considered configuration on φ1 and φ2, the HLIL distribution with parameter vector φ1 first-order stochastically dominates the HLIL distribution with parameter vector φ2.
family: half logistic inverse Lomax HLIL(α,λ,β): F(x;φ) = [1 − (1 − (1 + x/λ)^{−1})^{−α}]^β / [1 + (1 − (1 + x/λ)^{−1})^{−α}]^β, x > 0; λ scale, α, β shapes
compared: parameter vectors φ1 vs φ2 with componentwise orders α2 ≤ α1, λ1 ≤ λ2, β1 ≤ β2

quote: Also, we can use this result to show that, for β ∈ (0, 1], the HLIL distribution with parameter vector φ = (α, λ, β) first-order stochastically dominates the IL distribution with parameter vector (α, λ). Such property is not immediate for the case β > 1. [Appendix:] Also, for β ∈ (0, 1], the following inequality holds: For x > 0, F(x; φ) ≤ F(x; (α, 1, λ)) = G(x; α, λ) / (1 + (1 − (1 + x/λ)^{−1})^{−α}) ≤ G(x; α, λ). This proves the first-order stochastic dominance of the HLIL distribution over the IL distribution in this case.
family: HLIL(α,λ,β) vs parent inverse Lomax IL(α,λ) with cdf G(x;α,λ) = (1 + λ/x)^{−α}
compared: HLIL with β ∈ (0,1] vs IL (the β = 1 boundary case)
